# Fix WebSocket accept context state leaking between connections

- [x] You've read the [[Contributor Guide](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md)](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) and [[Code of Conduct](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/main/CODE-OF-CONDUCT.md)](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/main/CODE-OF-CONDUCT.md).
- [x] You've included unit or integration tests for your change, where applicable.
- [x] You've included inline docs for your change, where applicable.
- [x] There's an open issue for the PR that you are making.

Create a new `WebSocketAcceptContext` for each WebSocket acceptance.

## Description

`DefaultWebSocketManager.AcceptWebSocketAsync(string? subProtocol)` previously reused a static `WebSocketAcceptContext` when no subprotocol was specified.

Because `WebSocketAcceptContext` is mutable, components such as Interactive Server Components can modify properties such as `DangerousEnableCompression`. Reusing the same instance can cause those changes to persist and affect subsequent unrelated WebSocket connections.

This change removes the shared default context and creates a new `WebSocketAcceptContext` for each call to `AcceptWebSocketAsync`.

A regression test was also added to verify that enabling compression for one WebSocket connection does not leak into a subsequent connection using the default accept context.

The regression test was verified to:
- Fail against the existing implementation.
- Pass after applying this change.

Fixes #69652

> AI assistance was used to help prepare the pull request details.

Fix misleading error for synchronous async JS interop calls

## Description

Fixes #46811.

When a `[JSInvokable]` method returning `Task`, `Task<T>`, `ValueTask`, or `ValueTask<T>` is invoked synchronously from JavaScript, the synchronous dispatcher previously attempted to serialize the returned asynchronous value, resulting in a misleading serialization error.

This change detects asynchronous return types before invoking the method and throws a clear `InvalidOperationException` directing callers to use `invokeMethodAsync`.

The existing asynchronous JS interop path is unchanged.

### Changes

- Detect `Task` and `ValueTask` return types in the synchronous dispatcher.
- Throw a clear error before invoking the asynchronous method.

Issues.Body:
# [Blazor] Make DefaultComponentPropertyActivator composable

<!-- Thank you for submitting a pull request to our repo. -->

<!-- If this is your first PR in the ASP.NET Core repo, please run through the checklist
below to ensure a smooth review and merge process for your PR. -->

- [x] You've read the [Contributor Guide](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/main/CONTRIBUTING.md) and [Code of Conduct](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/main/CODE-OF-CONDUCT.md).
- [x] You've included unit or integration tests for your change, where applicable.
- [x] You've included inline docs for your change, where applicable.
- [x] There's an open issue for the PR that you are making. If you'd like to propose a new feature or change, please open an issue to discuss the change or find an existing issue.

<!-- Once all that is done, you're ready to go. Open the PR with the content below. -->

Enable custom `IComponentPropertyActivator` implementations to reuse default.

## Description

This PR introduces `DefaultComponentPropertyActivatorFactory.Create()`, enabling custom `IComponentPropertyActivator` implementations to compose and delegate to Blazor's default property activator.

`IComponentPropertyActivator` was introduced in #64596 by @javiercn to allow custom component property activation (e.g., integrations with custom DI containers, custom attribute bindings, or property-injection decorators).

### Problem solved 

In practice, custom property activators rarely want to re-implement all built-in Blazor property activation behavior from scratch (such as standard `[Inject]` handling, `[SupplyParameterFromKeyedServices]`, property reflection caching, and delegate compilation). Instead, they need to **compose** the framework's default behavior by delegating fallback property activation to it.

However, consumers attempting to compose the default activator faced two barriers:
1. **The concrete class is `internal`**: `DefaultComponentPropertyActivator` is internal to `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Components`, preventing direct instantiation or reference.
2. **It is not registered in the service provider**: `Renderer` currently resolves `IComponentPropertyActivator` from `IServiceProvider` optionally, falling back to creating an instance itself (`?? new DefaultComponentPropertyActivator()`). Because the default activator is not registered in the service container by any of the Blazor hosting extensions (`AddServerComponents`, `AddRazorComponents`, `WebAssemblyHostBuilder`, etc.), a custom activator cannot resolve it from DI either.

This left no mechanism for custom activators to access or reuse the default activator.

`DefaultComponentPropertyActivatorFactory.Create()` provides a public factory method that instantiates and returns `IComponentPropertyActivator` backed by the framework's default implementation:

```csharp
public class CustomPropertyActivator : IComponentPropertyActivator
{
    private readonly IComponentPropertyActivator _defaultActivator =
        DefaultComponentPropertyActivatorFactory.Create();

    public Action<IServiceProvider, IComponent> GetActivator(Type componentType)
    {
        var defaultAction = _defaultActivator.GetActivator(componentType);

        return (serviceProvider, component) =>
        {
            // Custom property activation logic here
            ...

            // Fallback / delegate to default activation logic
            defaultAction(serviceProvider, component);
        };
    }
}
```

### Reasoning for this approach

1. **Enables composition without public type exposure**: Keeps `DefaultComponentPropertyActivator` internal. Internal caching details, hot-reload cache invalidation (`ClearCache()`), and implementation mechanics remain fully encapsulated while exposing only the public contract (`IComponentPropertyActivator`).
2. **Minimal changes & zero churn across hosting platforms**: Avoids modifying DI registration entry points across all Blazor hosts (`Server`, `WebAssembly`, `Endpoints`, `WebView`).
3. **Preserves existing `Renderer` fallback behavior**: `Renderer` continues to use `serviceProvider.GetService<IComponentPropertyActivator>() ?? DefaultComponentPropertyActivatorFactory.Create()`. Renderers instantiated with custom or bare `IServiceProvider` instances (e.g., in unit tests or third-party render harnesses) continue working without requiring DI registration.
4. **Flexible lifetime management**: The consumer can choose to instantiate the factory-created activator as a singleton, hold it inside their own DI registration, or instantiate it on demand.

### Alternative approaches

1. **Registering `DefaultComponentPropertyActivator` under a separate interface in DI (e.g., `IDefaultComponentPropertyActivator`) and requiring it in `Renderer`**
   - *Disadvantages*: - Significant churn across the repository: requires adding service registrations to every Blazor hosting model (`AddRazorComponents`, `AddServerComponents`, `WebAssemblyHostBuilder`, `AddBlazorWebView`). - Breaking change for standalone renderers: any `Renderer` instantiated without a fully-configured DI container (such as unit test harnesses or custom embedding) would fail unless explicitly updated to provide the service. - Adds extra public interface surface area (`IDefaultComponentPropertyActivator`) solely for DI disambiguation.

2. **Registering the default activator as a Keyed Service in DI**
   - *Disadvantages*: - Requires keyed DI container support across all target environments. - Still requires updating every hosting platform's DI registration logic. - Does not help scenarios where custom property activators are instantiated outside DI or need a direct instance to compose.

3. **Making `DefaultComponentPropertyActivator` public with a public constructor**
   - *Disadvantages*: - Leaks concrete implementation details into the public API surface. - Constrains future internal refactoring of `DefaultComponentPropertyActivator`. - Risks consumers taking dependencies on non-contract behaviors or subclassing it.

4. **Base class with virtual methods (`ComponentPropertyActivatorBase`)**
   - *Disadvantages*: - Forces an inheritance model instead of composition. - Since `IComponentPropertyActivator.GetActivator` produces an `Action<IServiceProvider, IComponent>` delegate, chaining and delegating execution via composition is cleaner and avoids base-class state coupling.

### Tests

The existing tests already cover the behavior and still pass 

### Changes

- Added `DefaultComponentPropertyActivatorFactory` with public static method `Create() -> IComponentPropertyActivator`.
- Updated `Renderer.GetComponentPropertyActivatorOrDefault` to use `DefaultComponentPropertyActivatorFactory.Create()`.
- Updated existing tests to construct the default activator via the factory.
- Updated `PublicAPI.Unshipped.txt`.

Fixes #69657

Issues.Title: [OpenApi] Don't pass ignored property metadata to schema transformers for polymorphic discriminator nodes
Issues.Body:
Fixes #69080

## Problem

For a polymorphic type, the discriminator node can share its name with a `[JsonIgnore]`d property. `InnerApplySchemaTransformersAsync` matched nodes to `JsonTypeInfo.Properties` by name only, so transformers received the ignored property's `JsonPropertyInfo`/`JsonTypeInfo` for a node it doesn't describe. A transformer keying on the node's type could then rewrite the discriminator.

## Fix

Skip properties with no accessors (`Get: null, Set: null`), which is how System.Text.Json represents ignored properties. This matches how the schema emitter already excludes them.

In the name-collision case the discriminator node no longer triggers a transformer callback, which matches the no-collision behavior.

## Tests

- Added `SchemaTransformer_DoesNotReceiveIgnoredPropertyMetadataForPolymorphicDiscriminator`, using a base type with a `[JsonIgnore]`d property named like the discriminator.
- It fails without the fix (the transformer receives the ignored property's enum type) and passes with it.
- Full `Microsoft.AspNetCore.OpenApi.Tests`: 1034 passed, 5 pre-existing skips, 0 failed (run with `-p:UseIisNativeAssets=false` to avoid the local ANCM native build).

## AI assistance

I used AI assistance to explore the issue and draft the change. I reviewed the changes, ran the tests locally, and can explain them.

Issues.Title: PR reviewer (/review): follow-ups from real runs
Issues.Body:
2026-10-02T19:45:46Z
This issue collects follow-ups for the `review-pull-request` skill and the hosted `/review` workflow (`.github/workflows/pull-request-review.md`). Each item comes from a real run, with evidence. We'll keep adding items as more runs happen, then evaluate them together. Nothing here is decided yet.

## Runs so far (main reviewer from #69502, guidance `4449eb585c`)

| PR | Run | Result | Posted |
|---|---|---|---|
| #69505 | [37052985687](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/actions/runs/37052985687) | `NO_FINDINGS`; the only real bug was already reported in `discussion_r4153150961` | nothing |
| #68037 | [37054545721](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/actions/runs/37054545721) | `NO_FINDINGS`; existing feedback already covered the concerns | nothing |
| #67716 | [37054552964](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/actions/runs/37054552964) | 1 × P2 (a nonempty deferred value is replayed after switching to `type=file`) | 1 inline comment |
| #67746 | [37054561399](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/actions/runs/37054561399) | 1 × P3 (missing `<typeparam>` docs); the existing binary-compat finding was confirmed and not repeated | 1 inline comment |
| #69478 | [37054569267](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/actions/runs/37054569267) | 1 × P3 (default theme doesn't pad the footer cells) | 1 inline comment |

All five workers used `gpt-5.6-sol`. Both routed guides completed every time.

**Fork run of the #69634 reviewer** (head `3d478449d8` plus a one-line change to the fork guard only): [PureWeen/aspnetcore#119](https://github.com/PureWeen/aspnetcore/pull/119) reproduces #67716 at the same head `6cea93e0a2`, and [run 37056856055](https://github.com/PureWeen/aspnetcore/actions/runs/37056856055) passed all 9 jobs. The bundle carried `routing.md` with the expected hash, both guides were routed, and only `gpt-5.6-sol` ran. It posted 2 × P2:
- an empty-string checkbox `value` is treated as Boolean `true`. CCR raised this upstream in suppressed review 5019197421, so the upstream run skipped it as already reported.
- a stale `_blazorDeferredValue` replays when `type` changes. The upstream run left this unresolved; it hasn't been checked.

It did **not** report the upstream run's `type=file` P2. Same model, same PR head, different findings.

## Comparison with Copilot Code Review (CCR)

A read-only audit of the five upstream runs checked all 9 CCR root inline comments against the frozen heads:
- **CCR findings still live at the reviewed head:** 4 comments covering 3 root causes. The reviewer identified all 4 and skipped them as already reported. It missed 0.
- **Already fixed before the reviewed head:** 3. **Speculative or test-only:** 2.
- **New findings the reviewer posted that CCR didn't report:** 3 (the `type=file` exception, missing `TField` docs, footer padding). All 3 are supported by the source.
- **Demonstrated false positives:** 0 for CCR and 0 for the reviewer. Unverified is not the same as false.
- **Caveat:** the reviewer read the existing feedback before deciding, so this shows it identified CCR's findings, not that it would have found them on its own.

## Follow-ups

### 1. A "no findings" run is invisible on the PR
- **Evidence:** in #69505 run 37052985687, the agent emitted `noop` (`report-as-issue: false`, `status-comment: false`). The summary (duplicates already reported, one unresolved question) exists only in the run log. Nothing on the PR shows that a review ran.
- **Option:** post a short status comment for `NO_FINDINGS`. It would say the review completed, list feedback that was already reported, and list unresolved questions.

### 2. Components JS↔.NET compatibility rule isn't routed to the reviewer
- **Evidence:** the #69505 run left "mixed-version Boolean/integer acknowledgement compatibility" as UNRESOLVED, because "the frozen bundle contains no supported version-skew contract". **Correction:** an earlier version of this item said the rule wasn't bundled. It was. The producer exports the full source tree, including [`src/Components/AGENTS.md#javascript-and-net-compatibility-boundary`](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/4449eb585c8c82b5cf0e6f5d88f7ba73cbcadf62/src/Components/AGENTS.md#javascript-and-net-compatibility-boundary). That section says JS and .NET ship together, and that cross-major compatibility isn't required except on servicing branches. The reviewer didn't look it up, because no guide links to it. Under that rule, the question is not an actionable bug.
- **Option:** link that section from `docs/BlazorComponentsGuidance.md`, so it gets bundled.

### 3. Possible missed test-coverage finding on #69505 (unverified)
- **Evidence:** a blind, independent read-only review of #69505 at `960c3afb49` agreed with the hosted run on the main bug and on the dismissed "pending final flush" concern. It also raised a P3 that the hosted run didn't report: `src/Components/test/E2ETest/ServerExecutionTests/RemoteJSDataStreamTest.cs:34` doesn't force the second stream to hit backpressure while the first still needs chunks. So the browser test might pass even without the fix. This conclusion comes from reading the code only; the test wasn't run. The CCR audit agrees that the test source has no deterministic ordering barrier. Whether the test still passes with the fix reverted hasn't been observed.
- **Option:** confirm or refute it with a red/green run. If it's real, look at why the test-coverage check missed it.

### 4. Raw structured block in a published review body — fixed by #69634
- **Evidence:** the #69478 review body begins with `STATUS: FINDINGS  PR: ... HEAD_SHA: ... MERGE_BASE_SHA: ... GUIDANCE_SOURCE: ...`. That's internal bookkeeping in a public, contributor-facing summary.
- **Status:** the fork run of #69634's reviewer (see above) published a plain-prose review body with no raw `STATUS`/`HEAD_SHA` fields. This closes when #69634 merges.

### 5. Worker identity not reported by runtime
- **Evidence:** several worker results say "requested general-purpose / gpt-5.6-sol; runtime-reported type/model unknown". The model can only be confirmed from the log lines (`General-purpose(gpt-5.6-sol)`).
- **Option:** low priority. Decide whether a model check is needed at all.

### 6. No repeatable eval for review quality, so models can't be compared fairly
- **Evidence:** `eng/skill-evals/` has Vally evals for three other skills but none for `review-pull-request`. The 58 `PrepareReview.Tests` cover only the bundle producer, not review quality. Earlier quality checks were one-off runs on 5 PRs (#68365, #67969, #67616, #69484, #65504 as a no-findings control) with hand-checked answers, and they aren't in the repo. On #69505, `gpt-5.6-sol` and `gpt-6.1-sol` agreed on the main bug and differed only on minor points, so one run per model can't tell the models apart. The #67716 upstream run and the fork run differed in what they posted, on the same head and with the same model.
- **Live PRs aren't stable test inputs:** the reviewer skips anything already reported, and our own `/review` comments (for example on #67716) change what a later run will report. Heads also move, and `--head` then stops the run.
- **Option:** add `eng/skill-evals/review-pull-request/` with about 8–10 cases stored as frozen producer bundles, not live PRs, like the `pr-attention-queue` fixtures. Include known-bug PRs with one check per known finding, one or two clean PRs to catch false positives, a release-branch case like #69401, and one case that should end `BLOCKED`. Seed it with the hand-checked answers above and the labeled results from the runs in this issue. Then run the same cases with `gpt-5.6-sol`, `gpt-6.1-sol` and `gpt-6-astra`, several times each, and record quality, speed and cost.

### 7. A candidate left unresolved instead of being checked (#67716)
- **Evidence:** in run 37054552964, workers raised the stale `_blazorDeferredValue` replay after a later `type` change, but the final review left it unresolved for lack of browser evidence. The fork run posted the same concern as a P2. Either way, nobody checked it.
- **Option:** before leaving a candidate unresolved, name the exact missing contract or evidence, and take the smallest step that settles it. Exercise the real event and render path, not just the helper with a synthetic value. Don't drop a candidate just because a different finding in the same file was posted.

### 8. "Already reported" skips should name the comment and its current status
- **Evidence:** #68037 run 37054545721 skipped duplicate topics without naming the CCR comment IDs. Its final summary mixed one still-applicable suggestion with test and benchmark concerns that were already fixed. #67746 had two CCR comments about the same binary break, which should count as one root cause, not two.
- **Option:** for each skipped item, record which comment it matches (inline ID or review ID), the SHA that comment reviewed, whether it still applies at the frozen head, and which root cause it shares.


### 9. Small hosted-run noise that didn't change any result
- **Shell attempts:** the hosted workflow disables shell, but workers in all five runs still tried `jq`, checksum, or Python commands. They got `Permission denied` and fell back to reading files. This wastes turns, and a refused checksum command isn't evidence that a hash was verified. The fork run showed the same thing once. Option: tell hosted workers up front that only file-read tools are available.
- **Unclear wording, `SKILL.md` lines 100–102 at #69634's head:** "record unavailable runtime values as `unknown`, which alone does not make a guide incomplete" is followed by "unavailable agent type/model makes that guide `incomplete`." The intent is probably "the model can't be reported" versus "the requested model couldn't be started," but it reads like a contradiction. No run was marked incomplete because of it. Option: reword it.
- Not ours: every run logs an `awf-reflect` `EACCES` write failure in the gh-aw harness.


### 10. Red/green testing: the hosted reviewer is static today
Every finding so far is source-backed but not proven by running code. Locally, `SKILL.md` lets the coordinator optionally run a small repro in a temporary worktree, but has no "revert the fix" step. In the hosted workflow (`pull-request-review.md` lines 50–62), `bash: false`, `edit: false` and a `network` allow-list without the .NET SDK or NuGet feeds mean nothing gets built or run.

gh-aw can support this; it just isn't enabled. A follow-up would:
- build only the touched area (for example `src/Components/build.sh`), not the whole repo;
- run the PR's new or changed tests at head (expect pass), then with the non-test changes reverted to the merge base (expect fail);
- optionally write a minimal repro for a candidate finding (expect fail at head);
- record the exact commands and results in the review, and stay source-only, without reporting "no findings", when a build or test can't run;
- keep write tokens out of the job that runs PR code.

Open questions: runner disk and time for a scoped build, which feeds to allow, and a shell allow-list versus a deterministic build job that runs before the agent. Should be measured in the fork before any upstream PR.

# PR attention queue: treat pending-ci-rerun as a merge gate and dotnet-policy-service as a bot

<!-- Thank you for submitting a pull request to our repo. -->

<!-- If this is your first PR in the ASP.NET Core repo, please run through the checklist

<!-- Once all that is done, you're ready to go. Open the PR with the content below. -->

Treat pending-ci-rerun as a merge gate; recognize dotnet-policy-service as a bot

## Description

### Why

**`pending-ci-rerun` is a merge gate, not review routing.** The policy bot adds `pending-ci-rerun` to open, non-draft PRs after 7 days of inactivity and comments "please rerun validation before merging" ([`.github/policies/resourceManagement.yml:151-170`](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/cb9cc89cf8/.github/policies/resourceManagement.yml#L151-L170)). Pushes don't remove the label. Only an exact `/azp run` comment from a user with write access removes it ([`:678-690`](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/cb9cc89cf8/.github/policies/resourceManagement.yml#L678-L690)). Across the repo, 249 of 276 labeled open PRs are `REVIEW_REQUIRED`. The classifier sent every labeled PR to `WaitingOnCI` before it checked review state, so PRs that needed review or rescue were hidden there.

**`dotnet-policy-service` was treated as a human.** GraphQL returns the bare login `dotnet-policy-service`, without `[bot]`, so `Test-IsBotLogin` missed it. Its boilerplate comments wrongly triggered `non-author-discussion-requires-verification`, which kept PRs out of the review digest. They could also count as a human response in the community inbox, which hid neglected PRs.

### What changed

All changes are under `.github/skills/pr-attention-queue/`:

- **`scripts/PRAttentionQueue.psm1`**
  - Removed the `elseif ($ciRerunPending)` classifier branch that sent every labeled PR to `WaitingOnCI`.
  - Added a step that runs after classification. When the label is present, it adds `ci-rerun-pending` once as an informational reason. If the PR would otherwise be `ReadyToMerge`, it moves to `WaitingOnCI`, the next actor becomes `CI/automation`, and it gets the blocker `CI must be rerun before merge.` These PRs end up `not-candidate` for merge, because only `ReadyToMerge` items become candidates.
  - Because this step runs after all classification, `ci-rerun-pending` now also appears on `Draft` and `Excluded` (bot-authored) items.

This requires complete, untruncated evidence in which every collected comment is from a bot. Without this, adding the bot pattern alone left bot-only PRs at `unknown`. Incomplete or truncated evidence still gives `unknown`. Comments from other known bots, such as `github-actions`, also no longer prevent `no-response`.

Issues.Title: `DefaultWebSocketManager` reuses mutable accept context across WebSocket connections
Issues.Body:
`DefaultWebSocketManager.AcceptWebSocketAsync(string? subProtocol)` uses a static `WebSocketAcceptContext` when `subProtocol` is `null`.

Interactive Server Components modifies this context when accepting a `/_blazor` connection:

```csharp
context.DangerousEnableCompression = !compressionDisabled;
```

Because the context is shared, this value persists after the connection completes. A subsequent unrelated SignalR or application endpoint calling `AcceptWebSocketAsync()` can therefore inherit the modified compression setting.

**Expected behavior**: Each WebSocket connection has an independent accept context.

**Actual behavior**: Mutations made while accepting one connection can affect later connections that use the shared default context.

The default context should be created per acceptance or copied before being passed to `IHttpWebSocketFeature.AcceptAsync`.

Issues.Title: URL Rewrite identity rules re-decode `Request.Path`
Issues.Body:
A rewrite rule that matches `Request.Path` and re-emits the same captured segment (even a no-op/identity rule) can change the path value, because the rule matches against `Request.Path.ToString()` (escaped form) and reassigns via `PathString.FromUriComponent()` (decodes again). A path already containing a literal `%2e` (from Kestrel's normal single decode) becomes `..` after passing through the rule.

**Repro**

```csharp
app.UseRewriter(new RewriteOptions()
    .AddRewrite("^test/(.*)", "test/$1", skipRemainingRules: true));
app.Run(ctx => ctx.Response.WriteAsync(ctx.Request.Path));
```
Request: `GET /test/%252e%252e/secret`
- Before rewrite: `Request.Path` = `/test/%2e%2e/secret`
- After rewrite: `Request.Path` = `/test/../secret`

**Expected:** pass-through rewrite rule should not change `Request.Path`'s value.

Issues.Title: Certificate forwarding replaces ITlsConnectionFeature without preserving TLS channel binding
Issues.Body:
## Summary

When certificate forwarding replaces the request's `ITlsConnectionFeature`, the replacement does not implement `TryGetChannelBindingBytes`. The interface default returns `false`, so consumers such as the Negotiate handler observe "no channel binding available" on HTTPS requests whose underlying TLS connection does have one.

## What is wrong

* **Broken invariant:** changing where a request's client certificate comes from should not change the channel binding reported for the underlying connection. Today, the presence of the configured certificate header changes `TryGetChannelBindingBytes(ChannelBindingKind.Endpoint)` from `true` to `false` for the same connection.
* `ITlsConnectionFeature.TryGetChannelBindingBytes` was added in 11.0 (#67436) as a default interface method that returns `false`. Kestrel, HTTP.sys, and IIS in-process override it.
* `CertificateForwardingMiddleware.Invoke` sets a new `CertificateForwardingFeature` whenever the configured header is non-empty. The new feature does not keep the server's original feature, so the default implementation applies.
* Managed Negotiate (#68317) reads the binding from whichever `ITlsConnectionFeature` is current. When it returns `false`, `NegotiateState` constructs `NegotiateAuthentication` without `Binding`, so channel binding is not applied to that authentication exchange.
* The same pattern exists in IIS out-of-process integration (`ForwardedTlsConnectionFeature`) and in the Kestrel `ClientCertBufferingFeature` sample.

## Why it matters (defense in depth)

* **Correctness:** the channel binding result depends on an unrelated middleware and on whether a header is present. Negotiate degrades silently, with no log entry or failure, so the configuration looks protected while it is not.
* **Hardening:** channel binding was added to Negotiate in 11.0 so authentication is tied to the TLS connection. A middleware that only intends to change the client certificate source should not implicitly turn that protection off.
* **Extensibility:** because the method is a default interface member, any wrapper or replacement of `ITlsConnectionFeature` (framework, sample, or third-party) silently drops the binding unless it explicitly delegates.

## Affected code

* [src/Middleware/HttpOverrides/src/CertificateForwardingMiddleware.cs:47-55](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/4fe3a8c73edee50a26000a3f89a173db241765f5/src/Middleware/HttpOverrides/src/CertificateForwardingMiddleware.cs#L47-L55) - replaces the feature when the header is present
* [src/Middleware/HttpOverrides/src/CertificateForwardingFeature.cs:11-52](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/4fe3a8c73edee50a26000a3f89a173db241765f5/src/Middleware/HttpOverrides/src/CertificateForwardingFeature.cs#L11-L52) - no `TryGetChannelBindingBytes`, no reference to the original feature
* [src/Http/Http.Features/src/ITlsConnectionFeature.cs:24-53](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/4fe3a8c73edee50a26000a3f89a173db241765f5/src/Http/Http.Features/src/ITlsConnectionFeature.cs#L24-L53) - default implementation returns `false`
* [src/Security/Authentication/Negotiate/src/NegotiateHandler.cs:413-423](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/4fe3a8c73edee50a26000a3f89a173db241765f5/src/Security/Authentication/Negotiate/src/NegotiateHandler.cs#L413-L423) - reads the binding from the current feature
* [src/Security/Authentication/Negotiate/src/Internal/NegotiateState.cs:17-33](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/4fe3a8c73edee50a26000a3f89a173db241765f5/src/Security/Authentication/Negotiate/src/Internal/NegotiateState.cs#L17-L33) - empty token results in no `Binding`
* [src/Servers/IIS/IISIntegration/src/IISMiddleware.cs:145-152](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/4fe3a8c73edee50a26000a3f89a173db241765f5/src/Servers/IIS/IISIntegration/src/IISMiddleware.cs#L145-L152) - same replacement pattern
* [src/Servers/IIS/IISIntegration/src/ForwardedTlsConnectionFeature.cs:11-52](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/4fe3a8c73edee50a26000a3f89a173db241765f5/src/Servers/IIS/IISIntegration/src/ForwardedTlsConnectionFeature.cs#L11-L52) - same missing delegation
* [src/Servers/Kestrel/samples/SampleApp/ClientCertBufferingFeature.cs:32-76](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/4fe3a8c73edee50a26000a3f89a173db241765f5/src/Servers/Kestrel/samples/SampleApp/ClientCertBufferingFeature.cs#L32-L76) - sample wrapper without delegation

## Recommended fix

**Selected approach: delegate channel binding to the original feature.**

* In `CertificateForwardingMiddleware.Invoke`, capture `httpContext.Features.Get<ITlsConnectionFeature>()` before replacing it and pass it to `CertificateForwardingFeature`.
* Implement `TryGetChannelBindingBytes` in `CertificateForwardingFeature` by delegating to the captured feature; return `false` with an empty token when there is none.
* Apply the same change to `IISMiddleware` / `ForwardedTlsConnectionFeature`, and update the Kestrel `ClientCertBufferingFeature` sample to delegate.
* Update the XML docs on `ITlsConnectionFeature.TryGetChannelBindingBytes` to state that implementations which wrap or replace another `ITlsConnectionFeature` must delegate this method.
* Add a debug-level log in `NegotiateHandler` when `Request.IsHttps` is `true` but no channel binding is available, so the degraded mode is observable.

Both feature types are internal, so the selected approach has no public API change.

**Alternatives considered:**

* **Separate channel binding feature** (for example, a dedicated feature interface that certificate middleware never replaces). This is more robust against third-party wrappers, but it is a public API change that needs API review. `TryGetChannelBindingBytes` is still in `PublicAPI.Unshipped.txt`, so this remains possible before 11.0 GA and is worth discussing.
* **Fail closed in Negotiate** when `Request.IsHttps` is `true` and no binding is available. This would break servers that legitimately do not provide a binding (for example, HTTP.sys with legacy hardening), so it would need an opt-in option, which is also public API.
* **Documentation only.** This leaves the silent degradation in place.

**Compatibility considerations:**

* The delegated binding describes the TLS connection the server terminated (`tls-server-end-point` is derived from that server's certificate). Behind a TLS-terminating proxy, clients compute their binding from the certificate the proxy presented.
* Deployments where the proxy and backend present the same certificate behave the same with or without the forwarded header after the fix.
* Deployments where the certificates differ and Negotiate currently succeeds only because the binding is dropped will start failing after the fix. Owners should decide whether this needs a breaking-change note, documentation that channel binding is not supported behind TLS-terminating proxies, or an opt-out.
* The feature is new in 11.0 and has not shipped in a GA release, so fixing it before 11.0 GA avoids a behavior change after release.

## Acceptance criteria

* [ ] With certificate forwarding configured and the header present, `TryGetChannelBindingBytes` on the request's `ITlsConnectionFeature` returns the same result and bytes as the server's original feature.
* [ ] When there is no original feature, `TryGetChannelBindingBytes` returns `false` with an empty token.
* [ ] `CertificateForwardingTest` covers delegation with a fake original feature that provides a token, and covers the no-original-feature case.
* [ ] `IISMiddlewareTests` covers the same behavior for `ForwardedTlsConnectionFeature`.
* [ ] A `NegotiateHandlerTests` test runs `UseCertificateForwarding()` before authentication with the header present and asserts the Negotiate state receives the connection's non-empty binding. The test fails before the fix and passes after it.
* [ ] `NegotiateHandler` logs at debug level when an HTTPS request has no channel binding, with a test asserting the log.
* [ ] `ITlsConnectionFeature.TryGetChannelBindingBytes` XML docs describe the delegation requirement.
* [ ] The Kestrel `ClientCertBufferingFeature` sample delegates `TryGetChannelBindingBytes`.
* [ ] The compatibility decision for proxies presenting a different certificate is recorded (release note, docs, or opt-out).

Issues.Title: [Static assets] Missing mapped assets can return an empty 200 response from the Blazor development server
Issues.Body:
### Is there an existing issue for this?

- [x] I have searched the existing issues

Split from [#69488](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/69488). Client-side recovery is tracked in [#69644](https://github.com/dotnet/runtime/issues/135090).

### Describe the bug

The standalone Blazor WebAssembly dev server can return an empty `200 OK` when a mapped static asset is missing. The shared `StaticAssetsInvoker.Invoke` catches `FileNotFoundException`, calls `Response.Clear()`, and returns. Clearing resets the status to `200` and removes cache headers, allowing the invalid response to be cached.

### Expected Behavior

Return `404 Not Found` with `Cache-Control: no-store` when the mapped file cannot be opened before the response starts. Log the missing asset and cover uncompressed and compressed representations. This issue concerns server responses, not loader recovery.

### Steps To Reproduce

Using the .NET 10 standalone app from the parent issue:

1. Start the dev server, then temporarily rename the application's fingerprinted assembly and compressed copy.
2. Request the mapped asset with a fresh HTTP client. The report observes an empty `200`, rather than `404`.
3. Restore the files and confirm the server can serve them again.

### Exceptions (if any)

`FileNotFoundException` is caught without setting an error response.

### .NET Version

Reported with SDK 10.0.401 and runtime/packages 10.0.12. The same catch exists on main. The host reproduction is reporter-provided, supported by source inspection.

### Anything else?

See [`StaticAssetsInvoker.Invoke`](https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/blob/84e35658e5d7e0c0fea4af4e4ffb604c225a05dc/src/StaticAssets/src/StaticAssetsInvoker.cs#L150-L173). The implementation is shared with other `MapStaticAssets` hosts, so the scope may extend beyond the dev server.

Recreate missing temp directory before buffering bodies to disk

## Description

`AspNetCoreTempDirectory` caches `ASPNETCORE_TEMP` / `Path.GetTempPath()` for the process lifetime and previously threw `DirectoryNotFoundException` if that folder was missing. Cleanup tools or operators can still delete it after startup (including a “stable” `ASPNETCORE_TEMP` path). Later large form reads and buffered writes then fail until something outside the process recreates the directory.

This change keeps the cached path, but calls `Directory.CreateDirectory` on every lookup (no-op if it exists) and again immediately before creating `ASPNETCORE_*.tmp` in `FileBufferingReadStream` / `FileBufferingWriteStream`. Path selection is unchanged. This does not try to refresh `%TEMP%` or allocate a Windows session-id folder.

Distinct from #42647, which recommended pointing `ASPNETCORE_TEMP` at a directory that already exists.

Fixes #68622

Issues.Title: Document that WS-Federation remote sign-out (wsignoutcleanup1.0) is unauthenticated and how to restrict or disable it
Issues.Body:
## Summary

The XML docs for WS-Federation remote sign-out don't say that `wsignoutcleanup1.0` requests can't be verified as coming from the identity provider. Because of that, applications enable remote sign-out by default without knowing it can be triggered from any origin. This issue proposes a **documentation-only** resolution: describe that behavior and how to opt out or restrict it.

## What is wrong

* **Missing guidance:** `WsFederationHandler` processes every `GET` to `RemoteSignOutPath` with `wa=wsignoutcleanup1.0` by calling `SignOutAsync(SignOutScheme)`. The only gate is `OnRemoteSignOut`, which does nothing by default. That's inherent to the protocol: a `wsignoutcleanup1.0` message carries no session identifier, signature, or token, so the handler has nothing to verify. But none of this is documented.
* `RemoteSignOutPath` is enabled by default (`/signin-wsfed`, the same path as `CallbackPath`). Its XML doc only says "Requests received on this path will cause the handler to invoke SignOut using the SignOutScheme".
* The sign-in side documents its equivalent concern: the `AllowUnsolicitedLogins` docs explain why unsolicited logins are off by default. The sign-out side has no comparable explanation, and there's no matching option.

## Why it matters (defense in depth)

* **Correctness:** applications can't make an informed decision about whether to keep remote sign-out enabled, disable it, or restrict it.
* **Hardening:** documenting the opt-out and a restrictive `OnRemoteSignOut` pattern gives applications a supported way to limit which requests can end a session. No framework behavior change is needed.
* **Why docs-only rather than a code change:**
  * The protocol message has no session-binding value, so the framework can't add an OIDC-style `sid` check.
  * Making unsolicited sign-out opt-in would silently break ADFS single sign-out for existing applications.
  * Both extensibility points needed to mitigate already exist (`RemoteSignOutPath`, `OnRemoteSignOut`).

## Affected code

* `src/Security/Authentication/WsFederation/src/WsFederationOptions.cs:36-41`: constructor defaults. `RemoteSignOutPath = "/signin-wsfed"`, with a comment noting that Entra ID sends cleanup messages to a non-deterministic reply URL.
* `src/Security/Authentication/WsFederation/src/WsFederationOptions.cs:182-190`: `AllowUnsolicitedLogins` docs (the precedent) and `RemoteSignOutPath` docs (the gap).
* `src/Security/Authentication/WsFederation/src/WsFederationEvents.cs:26-29` and `56-59`: `OnRemoteSignOut` and `RemoteSignOut` docs ("Invoked when a wsignoutcleanup request is received…").
* `src/Security/Authentication/WsFederation/src/WsFederationHandler.cs:67-79`: `HandleRequestAsync` routes matching `GET` requests to remote sign-out.
* `src/Security/Authentication/WsFederation/src/WsFederationHandler.cs:466-498`: `HandleRemoteSignOutAsync` raises the event, then signs out.
* Conceptual docs in dotnet/AspNetCore.Docs: the WS-Federation authentication article.

## Recommended fix

**Selected approach: documentation only, in two places.**

1. **XML docs in this repo:**
   * **`WsFederationOptions.RemoteSignOutPath`:** add `<remarks>`:
     * `wsignoutcleanup1.0` messages carry no session identifier or signature, so the handler can't verify that a request came from the identity provider. Requests from any origin are processed.
     * If single sign-out from the identity provider isn't required, set this property to `PathString.Empty` to disable remote sign-out. This is the recommended choice for Microsoft Entra ID, which doesn't send cleanup messages to a deterministic path.
     * Otherwise, use `WsFederationEvents.OnRemoteSignOut` to accept only requests that match how the identity provider delivers cleanup messages.
   * **`WsFederationEvents.OnRemoteSignOut` / `RemoteSignOut`:** add `<remarks>` explaining that calling `HandleResponse()` or `SkipHandler()` prevents the sign-out. Add an `<example>` with this pattern:

     ```csharp
     options.Events.OnRemoteSignOut = context =>
     {
         // Accept cleanup only when the request comes from the identity provider's origin.
         var referer = context.Request.Headers.Referer.ToString();
         if (!referer.StartsWith("https://adfs.contoso.com/", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))
         {
             context.HandleResponse();
         }
         return Task.CompletedTask;
     };
     ```

     The example's remarks must state:
     * A **missing `Referer` is rejected deliberately.** Allowing an empty value defeats the check.
     * The comparison includes the **trailing `/`**, so look-alike hosts don't match.
     * Applications should **check what their identity provider actually sends** before enforcing a filter (for example `Referer`, `Sec-Fetch-Dest`, and `Sec-Fetch-Site` on a real ADFS sign-out), because a wrong filter silently breaks single sign-out.
     * Iframe- or image-based cleanup from the identity provider generally requires the authentication cookie to use `SameSite=None` to be effective.
2. **Conceptual docs (dotnet/AspNetCore.Docs):** add a "Remote sign-out" section to the WS-Federation article with the same guidance and sample, plus a link to the API docs. File a linked issue in that repo.

**Alternatives considered:**

* **Add an `AllowUnsolicitedSignOut` option (default `false`).** Rejected for now: it's a breaking change for ADFS single sign-out, and the protocol gives the framework nothing to validate beyond request metadata.
* **Built-in `Referer` or `Sec-Fetch-*` filtering.** Rejected: legitimate delivery differs between identity providers and deployments (iframe vs. image vs. top-level, referrer policy). A framework default would be either too loose or would break real deployments.
* **Disable remote sign-out by default.** Rejected: breaking change for existing ADFS deployments.

**Compatibility, migration, and versioning:**

* No runtime behavior change and no public API change, so no API review is needed. Documentation can ship in any release.
* An option-based approach could be revisited separately in a future major version.

## Acceptance criteria

* [ ] The `WsFederationOptions.RemoteSignOutPath` XML docs state that cleanup requests can't be verified as coming from the identity provider, and describe disabling with `PathString.Empty`, including the Entra ID note.
* [ ] The `WsFederationEvents.OnRemoteSignOut` and `RemoteSignOut` XML docs describe `HandleResponse()` / `SkipHandler()` as the way to reject a request, and include the `<example>` above with its remarks (missing `Referer` rejected, trailing `/`, verify against the real identity provider, `SameSite=None` note).
* [ ] A linked dotnet/AspNetCore.Docs issue or PR adds a "Remote sign-out" section to the WS-Federation article.
* [ ] No changes to runtime behavior or `PublicAPI.*.txt`.

# Route PR review guides from a table and harden review preparation and publishing

## Description

Follow-up to #69502, which added the PR review skill. Its `prepare-review.cs` script freezes a PR into a read-only bundle (the diff, the source at the head and base commits, and the guidance files), and the reviewer reads only that bundle. This PR changes how the bundle picks guides, and tightens how it is built and how results are published by the hosted `/review` workflow. The review criteria in the guides are unchanged, and there are no product code changes.

### What changes in practice

- **Adding a review area is one table row plus its guide file.** `.github/skills/review-pull-request/routing.md` now says which guide applies to which changed paths. Today that is `docs/CrossCuttingGuidance.md` for every PR and `docs/BlazorComponentsGuidance.md` for `src/Components/`. Before, the producer hard-coded the guide list and the `src/Components/` check. Now it only reads the table.
- **A review that can't finish says so.** When the agent can't finish, the hosted workflow posts one short comment on the PR: `Review not published (<STATUS>): <reason>` followed by `No partial findings were published.`, where the status is `BLOCKED` or `INCOMPLETE`. Before, nothing was posted to the PR. If bundle preparation itself fails, the run still stops before the agent starts and posts nothing.
- **Findings are shorter.** Each one is a one-line claim, `file:line`, severity, a minimal repro, at most two lines of impact, and a fix snippet when possible. Hosted inline comments use the same shape.
- **Local reviews can optionally try a repro.** A native local review may create a temporary detached worktree at the reviewed commit, run a small test there, and remove it. A failing repro confirms a finding; a passing one counts as evidence against it. If that isn't possible, the review stays source-only. Hosted runs and workers never execute target code.

### Bundle producer (`prepare-review.cs`)

- **Routing table rules.**
  - The table comes from the guidance copy the reviewer uses, never from the PR being reviewed, so a PR can't change its own routing.
  - `*` applies to every PR. Any other prefix ends in `/` and matches at a directory boundary. A row matches if either the new or the previous file name starts with its prefix.
  - More than one row can match, and guides are de-duplicated.
  - A missing, empty or malformed table, a missing `*` row, a duplicate row, or a missing or invalid guide returns `BLOCKED`.
  - The table's path and SHA-256 are recorded in the manifest, and `--check` verifies them. The manifest stays at version 2; bundles without the new `routing` object are rejected.
- **No area-specific skip rule.** The producer no longer skips three Components-only policy links for non-Components PRs. Links in every routed guide are now handled the same way. With today's guides this changes nothing, because only the Components guide links them.
- **Bounded process output.** Output from child processes is counted while it is read. Past the existing 64 MiB limit, the process tree is killed and the producer returns the existing `BLOCKED` error. Before, both streams were fully buffered before the size check.
- **`--check` re-reads the PR.** After validating a bundle, `--check` re-reads the PR from GitHub and fails if the head or base commit moved, as preparation already does.
- **One retry.** If the target or base moves during preparation, the producer discards its partial output and rebuilds once. A second move or any other failure returns `BLOCKED`. `--check` never retries.

The output limit and the `--check` re-read address the review comments on #69502.

### Skill (`SKILL.md`)

- Guides, policies and context files under `guidance.root` are read with the `.source` suffix, matching how the producer writes them.
- Each routed guide gets exactly one fresh worker. Corrections go to that same worker; if that isn't possible, the guide is recorded as incomplete instead of being relaunched or replaced.
- For the generic `Permission denied and could not request permission from user` error, the reviewer tells the user to rerun interactively or with `--allow-all-paths`. It no longer claims the error proves a long path.
- The routing, optional local repro and finding format changes described above.

### Hosted workflow (`pull-request-review.md` and `.lock.yml`)

- **Second head check at publish time.** Before publishing, the workflow re-reads the live PR inside the publishing job (a `jobs.safe_outputs.pre-steps` hook). It blocks publication if the head moved, the PR closed, or the base repository changed. The earlier `verify_live_head` job stays as a fail-fast gate. A push can still land between the check and the write; if it does, the review stays attached to the commit that was reviewed.
- **Status comment.** This adds one capped `add_comment` output, limited to the triggering PR, used only for the status comment described above.
- **The agent output is validated before anything is published.** The job fails unless the output is a JSON object with no reported errors and only known item types, and is exactly one of:
  - one review with 1 to 5 inline comments;
  - one `noop`;
  - one incomplete report (`report_incomplete`, `missing_data` or `missing_tool`) with a single-line reason of 1 to 240 characters, plus one status comment that uses the fixed text above with that same reason.

## Validation

- **C# tests:** `dotnet run --project .github/skills/review-pull-request/scripts/PrepareReview.Tests.csproj` passes 61 of 61 on macOS at the current head. The last Windows run was 58 of 58 at `3d478449d8`; it has not been repeated since the last two commits.
- **Publication gate:** `node .github/workflows/tests/pull-request-review-publication-preflight.test.mjs` runs 46 cases against both the workflow source and the compiled lock. They cover malformed, empty, mixed, duplicate and unknown outputs, non-empty `errors`, and mismatched status text.
- **Tests fail without the change:**
  - With the old producer restored, 11 routing test cases failed. With the new one, all pass.
  - The earlier output-limit, `--check` re-read and retry tests each failed with their fix removed.
  - For the removed skip rule, 3 new test cases failed before the change and pass after.
- **Real PRs:** at `3d478449d8`, #69522 (`release/11.0`), #69505 (Components) and #69585 (MVC) chose the same guides, policies and context as the current `main` producer. For the last commit, the old and new producers produced the same bundle for #67716, #69585 and #69308, apart from the producer hash and timings.
- **Workflow compile:** gh-aw v0.89.21 `compile pull-request-review --strict` produced identical lock files on two runs (SHA-256 `f28d54e46fe8c8b2b6041d604f37e41f29a7b1438c3926542db6adf84cd8f3c9`). `.github/aw/actions-lock.json` is unchanged.
- **Hosted runs, on a fork only:**
  - A normal run (37056856055) on a copy of #67716, at `3d478449d8` plus a fork-only guard, passed every job, read the routing table and posted one COMMENT review with two findings.
  - A forced-incomplete run (36916516447), at `9be41d75dd`, posted one status comment and no review, and ended in `failure` by design.
  - The saved agent outputs of both runs pass the final publication gate unchanged.
- **Local native runs** on four PRs, before the routing, local repro and finding format changes, confirmed that workers read `.source` paths and that each guide got exactly one worker.
- **Not run:** a hosted or native review of the final head, a native run of the optional local repro, and a Windows rerun of the C# tests.

Issues.Title: OIDC remote sign-out signs out even when SignOutScheme authenticates no session, bypassing sid/iss binding
Issues.Body:
## Summary

`OpenIdConnectHandler.HandleRemoteSignOutAsync` skips its `sid`/`iss` session-binding checks whenever `SignOutScheme` doesn't authenticate the request, and still calls `SignOutAsync`. So the binding the handler is designed to enforce only applies when the browser happens to send the authentication cookie with the remote sign-out request.

## What is wrong

* **Broken invariant:** a remote sign-out should only end a session after the request has been checked against that session's identifier (`sid`) and issuer (`iss`), whenever the session carries them. Today the checks run only if the incoming request carries a readable authentication ticket. When it doesn't, the handler treats "no ticket visible" the same as "the session has no `sid`" and goes ahead with `SignOutAsync(SignOutScheme)`.
* **Origin:** the fallback was added in 2016, together with the `sid` check, on top of an endpoint that previously checked nothing. The code comment justifies it as "the authentication cookie was already cleared". That assumption predates the `SameSite=Lax` default on the authentication cookie (`CookieAuthenticationOptions`). Under current browser cookie policies, the cookie can be withheld from requests to `RemoteSignOutPath` while the session still exists. A missing ticket no longer reliably means there's no session.
* **Side effect:** with the default cookie `SignOutScheme`, `CookieAuthenticationHandler.HandleSignOutAsync` always emits a deletion `Set-Cookie`, even if the request had no cookie. So a request the handler couldn't bind to any session can still clear that session's cookie in the browser.

## Why it matters (defense in depth)

* **Correctness:** the `sid` binding is the handler's only mechanism for telling a genuine provider logout notification apart from an unsolicited one. Its effectiveness currently depends on browser cookie-attachment rules rather than on the handler's own logic. This holds even for identity providers that issue `sid`.
* **Hardening:** `RemoteSignOutPath` intentionally runs without the cross-origin CSRF verdict (#68669). That PR's safety rationale (`state` plus a correlation cookie, nonce, PKCE) covers `CallbackPath`, not `RemoteSignOutPath`, which has no equivalent protection. The `sid`/`iss` binding is the remaining boundary on this endpoint, and it should hold independently of whether the cookie was attached.
* **No-op in practice:** when no ticket is present, `SignOutAsync` has no server-side effect. There's no session key, so the `SessionStore` isn't touched. Its only observable effect is the deletion header. Skipping it removes no meaningful legitimate functionality.

## Affected code

* `src/Security/Authentication/OpenIdConnect/src/OpenIdConnectHandler.cs:90-105`: `HandleRequestAsync` routes `RemoteSignOutPath` through `RemoteAuthenticationAntiforgery.HandleWithoutAntiforgeryVerdictAsync`.
* `src/Security/Authentication/OpenIdConnect/src/OpenIdConnectHandler.cs:165-210`: `HandleRemoteSignOutAsync` authenticates `SignOutScheme`, runs the `sid`/`iss` checks only when the claims are present, then calls `SignOutAsync`. The null-principal path falls through to sign-out.
* `src/Security/Authentication/Cookies/src/CookieAuthenticationHandler.cs:382-420`: `HandleSignOutAsync` calls `CookieManager.DeleteCookie` unconditionally.
* `src/Security/Authentication/Cookies/src/CookieAuthenticationOptions.cs:19`: the default `SameSite = SameSiteMode.Lax`.
* `src/Shared/RemoteAuthenticationAntiforgery.cs`: the verdict-suppression rationale, which applies to callback paths.
* `src/Security/Authentication/test/OpenIdConnect/OpenIdConnectEventTests.cs:1002-1019` and `OpenIdConnectEventTests_Handler.cs:1002-1019`: `OnRemoteSignOut_Invoked` currently asserts that a request with no cookie produces a deletion `Set-Cookie`.
* `src/Security/Authentication/test/OpenIdConnect/OpenIdConnectTests.cs:303-376`: the existing `sid`/`iss` remote sign-out tests. All of them send the cookie.

## Recommended fix

**Selected approach:** in `HandleRemoteSignOutAsync`, keep the full `AuthenticateResult` from `Context.AuthenticateAsync(Options.SignOutScheme)` instead of only `?.Principal`. If the result is `None` (no ticket presented), log a new debug event (for example `RemoteSignOutNoSession`) and return `true` without calling `SignOutAsync`. Leave everything else unchanged:

* `Succeeded` with `sid`/`iss`: bind as today.
* `Succeeded` without `sid`/`iss`: sign out as today. This preserves the "lossy cookie conversion" and "provider doesn't support sessions" cases from the existing comment.
* `Failure` (a cookie was presented but is invalid or expired): sign out as today. The cookie was sent, so clearing it is legitimate cleanup.
* The `RemoteSignOut` event still runs first, unchanged, so applications keep full control through `HandleResponse()` and `SkipHandler()`.

Also update the code comment at lines 165-169, which currently lists "cookie already cleared" as a reason to bypass the checks.

**Alternatives considered:**

* **Fail closed whenever `sid` is missing, even with an authenticated principal.** Rejected: it breaks legitimate remote sign-out for identity providers without session management, which the current fallback exists to support.
* **Bind on `iss` alone, or retain the raw `iss` claim by default.** Rejected: `iss` is the same for every session from a given provider, so it isn't a session-binding value.
* **Restrict `RemoteSignOutPath` by HTTP method.** Rejected as the primary fix: it's protocol-dependent, and it doesn't address the underlying property that a request without a visible session can still end one.
* **Re-apply the cross-origin CSRF verdict to `RemoteSignOutPath`.** Rejected: legitimate logout notifications are cross-site by design. This is why #68669 suppressed the verdict.

**Compatibility, migration, and versioning:**

* This is a behavior change in shipped code. Requests that carry no readable ticket will no longer produce a deletion `Set-Cookie`. Affected scenarios:
  * Custom `SignOutScheme` handlers whose `AuthenticateAsync` returns `None` but whose sign-out performs work.
  * Apps relying on `CookieAuthenticationEvents.OnSigningOut` firing for cookie-less remote sign-out.
  * Any identity provider that delivers logout notifications in a way that never carries the application's cookie. Those apps can restore the old behavior through `OnRemoteSignOut`, or by configuring the cookie to be sent (`SameSite=None`, which is already required for iframe-based front-channel logout to clear cookies).
* Add an `AppContext` switch (for example `Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.OpenIdConnect.AllowRemoteSignOutWithoutSession`) to restore the legacy behavior. Document it as a breaking change for the target release.
* No public API change is required unless the team prefers an `OpenIdConnectOptions` property over an `AppContext` switch. That would need API review.
* Consider whether to service this, given the change in observable behavior. Otherwise target the next major release.

## Acceptance criteria

* [ ] A remote sign-out request for which `SignOutScheme` returns `AuthenticateResult.None` does not call `SignOutAsync` and emits no `Set-Cookie`.
* [ ] With an authenticated principal carrying `sid`, existing binding behavior is unchanged: a missing or mismatched `sid` leaves the session intact, and a matching `sid` signs out.
* [ ] With an authenticated principal without `sid`/`iss`, sign-out still occurs (compatibility with session-less providers).
* [ ] With a presented but invalid or expired ticket (`AuthenticateResult.Failure`), sign-out still clears the cookie.
* [ ] The `RemoteSignOut` event is still raised before the session check, and `HandleResponse()` / `SkipHandler()` behave as today.
* [ ] `OnRemoteSignOut_Invoked` is updated in both `OpenIdConnectEventTests.cs` and `OpenIdConnectEventTests_Handler.cs`, and new tests cover each row above for both GET and form POST remote sign-out.
* [ ] The legacy-behavior switch is covered by a test and documented, along with a breaking-change notice.

This is more of a question but its not enough of a question that i could post it up on stack overflow without risking it just getting closed as primary opinion based or to broad.   So i am going to put it here in hopes of getting an answer.

The issue is the understanding of how remember me is supposed to work.    My problem is that its not doing what we would expect it to do.   

Management expects when a user logs in and clicks remember me that they will then not be required to type their login and password again for a month.  Whether or not they will still have to type in the 2fa code is up for debate.

What is actually happening is that i can close the browser reboot and come back for about an hour and 15 minutes and then i will be forced to type my password again.    This still happens even with a valid `.AspNetCore.Identity.Application` cookie set that is not due to expire for another month.

After digging around in the code i found that Remember me is actually isPersistent and it is defined as.

>Flag indicating whether the sign-in cookie should persist after the browser is closed.

Which brings you to:

There are two different types of Cookies:

- session cookies, held in memory, and which expire once the browser exits
- persistent cookies, which have a time-to-live, are persisted on disk, and are sent by the browser until their time-to-live has elapsed.

All this being said remember machine 2fa works as expected i am not prompted again for the 2fa and i have a cookie on my machine `Identity.TwoFactorRememberMe`.

So I guess my question is why are we not getting a `Identity.FactorRememberMe` or why isn't sign in respecting a long life time of the `AspNetCore.Identity.Application` cookie?

How is this supposed to work exactly?   I am following the code here even though we have normal MVC and not razor pages like you have in the example.  I am still just calling 

>var signInUserResult = await _signInManager.PasswordSignInAsync(userName, password, rememberMe, true);

Note: I am using Asp .net Identity in Identity server 4 application.

Issues.Title: Should IdentityUser be in the EntityFramework namespace?
Issues.Body:
https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/dotnet/api/microsoft.aspnetcore.identity.entityframeworkcore.identityuser?view=aspnetcore-1.1

I'm looking through various implementations from the [readme](https://github.com/aspnet/Identity/blob/master/README.md) and I've noticed they all use `IdentityUser ` for their concrete type to pass to `UserManager`, or have had to craft a custom type to be able to have a contract between the database and the .NET AspNetIdentity implentation they've written (see the DynamoDB library).

I've had to do this too for the [Marten implementation I've written](https://github.com/yetanotherchris/Marten.AspNetIdentity), and the reason is, a `TUser` that your `UserStore` takes, should really be an interface - it will always have an email, most likely an Id of some sort, firstname, lastname and then a bag of properties.

Things become even more abstract when dealing with claims.

If everyone is using `IdentityUser` or their own custom `TUser` doesn't this defeat the purpose of AspnetIdentity - which is to be able to switch and change implementations easily? That isn't possible if your consumer is tightly coupled with a `TUser` implementation of the library.

### Example `TUser` implementations

- [MongoIdentityUser](https://github.com/tugberkugurlu/AspNetCore.Identity.MongoDB/blob/master/src/AspNetCore.Identity.MongoDB/MongoIdentityUser.cs)
- [DynamoIdentityUser](https://github.com/miltador/AspNetCore.Identity.DynamoDB/blob/master/src/AspNetCore.Identity.DynamoDB/DynamoIdentityUser.cs)
- [Redis uses `IdentityUser<string>`](https://github.com/aguacongas/Identity.Redis/blob/develop/src/Aguacongas.Identity.Redis/UserStore.cs)
Issues.RelatedDescription: Closed issue "Should IdentityUser be in the EntityFramework namespace?" (#2056)

Issues.Body:
I used to be able to use `dotnet watch` in Visual Studio by adding the following section to `launchSettings.json` and starting the project without debugging using CTRL + F5.

```
    "Kestrel (dotnet watch run)": {
      "commandName": "Executable",
      "executablePath": "C:\\Program Files\\dotnet\\dotnet.exe",
      "commandLineArgs": "watch run",
      "launchBrowser": true,
      "launchUrl": "https://localhost:5001/",
      "environmentVariables": {
        "ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT": "Development"
      }
    },
```

This used to work in ASP.NET Core 1.1 but no longer does. According to https://github.com/aspnet/DotNetTools/issues/404 the new format for ASP.NET Core 2.0 is:

```
   "Kestrel (dotnet watch run)": {
      "commandName": "Executable",
      "executablePath": "C:\\Program Files\\dotnet\\dotnet.exe",
      "commandLineArgs": "watch run",
      "workingDirectory": "C:\\Users\\namc\\source\\repos\\WebApplication2\\WebApplication2",
      "launchBrowser": true,
      "launchUrl": "https://localhost:5001/",
      "environmentVariables": {
        "ASPNETCORE_ENVIRONMENT": "Development"
      }
    }
```

The problem with this is the hard coded `executablePath` which is Windows specific and the `workingDirectory` which is specific to wherever I did a Git clone on my local machine.

Issues.Title: [Breaking change]: OpenID Connect max_age validates auth_time
Issues.Body:
### Description

Starting in ASP.NET Core 11, the OpenID Connect handler validates the signed ID token `auth_time` claim whenever `OpenIdConnectOptions.MaxAge` or `OpenIdConnectChallengeProperties.MaxAge` causes an effective `max_age` value to be sent.

This change was introduced by https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/69321 and addresses https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/issues/67462.

### Version

.NET 11 RC 2

### Previous behavior

The handler sent `max_age` on the authorization request but did not validate the returned ID token's `auth_time`. Applications relied entirely on the identity provider to honor the request. A missing, malformed, stale, or excessively future `auth_time` did not cause authentication to fail.

### New behavior

When an effective `max_age` is sent, the handler correlates the exact value through protected authorization-transaction state and validates every ID token used by the supported authorization flow after normal token and OpenID Connect protocol validation.

The `auth_time` claim must be an integral, nonnegative OpenID Connect NumericDate. Authentication fails when the claim is missing, malformed, fractional, negative, overflowed, later than the current time plus `OpenIdConnectOptions.TokenValidationParameters.ClockSkew`, or older than `max_age` plus that clock skew. Exact boundaries and values within skew are accepted.

The validation covers authorization-code, implicit, and hybrid flows, including both relevant ID tokens in hybrid flows, and both the default `TokenHandler` path and legacy `SecurityTokenValidator` path. No validation occurs when no `max_age` is configured. In addition to the `MaxAge` properties, applications can configure the parameter through `AdditionalAuthorizationParameters` or `OnRedirectToIdentityProvider`.

### Type of breaking change

- [ ] **Binary incompatible**: Existing binaries may encounter a breaking change in behavior, such as failure to load or execute, and if so, require recompilation.
- [ ] **Source incompatible**: When recompiled using the new SDK or component or to target the new runtime, existing source code may require source changes to compile successfully.
- [x] **Behavioral change**: Existing binaries may behave differently at run time.

### Reason for change

OpenID Connect Core requires the authorization server to include `auth_time` when `max_age` is requested and recommends that the relying party validate it. Correlating and checking the signed assertion prevents a missing or nonconforming assertion from silently satisfying an application's configured maximum authentication age.

The guarantee remains limited to the trusted identity provider's signed assertion. ASP.NET Core cannot prove that a particular physical authentication ceremony occurred and cannot protect against a compromised identity provider that signs false data. This change does not revalidate UserInfo, refresh-token redemption, local cookie lifetime, or physical user interaction.

### Recommended action

Ensure that identity providers emit a valid signed `auth_time` and honor the requested `max_age` whenever the application configures that parameter, most commonly through `OpenIdConnectOptions.MaxAge` or `OpenIdConnectChallengeProperties.MaxAge`.

For a temporarily incompatible provider, restore the previous request-only behavior by setting the process-wide compatibility switch before authentication starts:

```csharp
AppContext.SetSwitch(
    "Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.OpenIdConnect.DisableMaxAgeValidation",
    true);
```

The equivalent runtime configuration is:

```json
{
  "runtimeOptions": {
    "configProperties": {
      "Microsoft.AspNetCore.Authentication.OpenIdConnect.DisableMaxAgeValidation": true
    }
  }
}
```

The switch defaults to `false` and is intended only as a temporary provider-compatibility escape hatch.

When pushed authorization is used, set or modify `max_age` in `OnRedirectToIdentityProvider`. Changing it later in `OnPushAuthorization` is rejected while validation is active unless pushing is skipped, because the handler has already correlated the value with the authorization response.

### Affected APIs

No public API signatures change. The behavioral change affects applications that set:

- `OpenIdConnectOptions.MaxAge`
- `OpenIdConnectChallengeProperties.MaxAge`
- `OpenIdConnectOptions.AdditionalAuthorizationParameters` when it includes `max_age`
- `OpenIdConnectEvents.OnRedirectToIdentityProvider` when it sets `max_age`

Issues.Title: [Breaking change]: Identity external login keys use ordinal equality
Issues.Body:
### Description

Starting in ASP.NET Core 11, the built-in Entity Framework Core Identity stores verify external-login `LoginProvider` and `ProviderKey` values using managed ordinal equality after the indexed database lookup returns a candidate.

This change was introduced by https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/69277.

### Version

.NET 11 RC 2

### Previous behavior

`UserStore` and `UserOnlyStore` filtered external logins with a database-translated equality predicate. The database collation therefore determined whether the stored `(LoginProvider, ProviderKey)` tuple matched the supplied values.

On a case-insensitive collation, `FindByLoginAsync` could resolve a login whose provider name or provider key differed only by case. On databases where equality ignores trailing spaces, it could also resolve a key that differed by trailing spaces. `RemoveLoginAsync` used the same collation-dependent lookup and could remove such a login.

### New behavior

The database equality remains the indexed candidate lookup. The built-in EF Identity stores then require the returned `LoginProvider` and `ProviderKey` to match the requested values using `StringComparison.Ordinal`.

A collation-only match now causes `FindByLoginAsync` to return no user and `RemoveLoginAsync` to perform no removal. Exact ordinal matches continue to work.

### Type of breaking change

- [ ] **Binary incompatible**: Existing binaries may encounter a breaking change in behavior, such as failure to load or execute, and if so, require recompilation.
- [ ] **Source incompatible**: When recompiled using the new SDK or component or to target the new runtime, existing source code may require source changes to compile successfully.
- [x] **Behavioral change**: Existing binaries may behave differently at run time.

### Reason for change

External provider keys are opaque identifiers whose equality must not vary with the configured database provider or collation. Managed ordinal verification makes the built-in EF stores consistent with the in-memory reference store while preserving the existing indexed database lookup.

### Recommended action

Ensure that applications persist and later supply the exact `LoginProvider` and `ProviderKey` values issued for an external login. Do not normalize, case-fold, trim, or otherwise alter provider keys.

Third-party `IUserLoginStore<TUser>` implementations own their equality semantics. Implementations that query a collation-aware database should preserve an indexed candidate lookup and verify the materialized provider name and key with ordinal equality before resolving or removing a login.

### Affected APIs

No public API signatures change. This behavioral change affects the built-in Entity Framework Core implementations of:

- `IUserLoginStore<TUser>.FindByLoginAsync`
- `IUserLoginStore<TUser>.RemoveLoginAsync`

Issues.Title: [Breaking change]: Blazor server-side rendering defers antiforgery validation to middleware
Issues.Body:
### Description

Starting in ASP.NET Core 11, Blazor static server-side rendering (SSR) endpoints no longer validate antiforgery tokens themselves. They rely on the antiforgery verdict recorded by upstream middleware and generate antiforgery tokens only when token-based antiforgery middleware is present.

This change was introduced by https://github.com/dotnet/aspnetcore/pull/67082.

### Version

.NET 11 Preview 6

### Previous behavior

When a Blazor SSR endpoint handled a form `POST`, the endpoint validated the request itself if antiforgery middleware hadn't already recorded a result.

The endpoint also generated and stored antiforgery tokens for rendered forms even when `app.UseAntiforgery()` wasn't present in the pipeline.

Consequently, apps that didn't call `app.UseAntiforgery()` still emitted and validated antiforgery tokens.

### New behavior

Blazor SSR endpoints now trust the `IAntiforgeryValidationFeature` verdict recorded by upstream middleware. A form `POST` is rejected with `400 Bad Request` when the recorded verdict is invalid.

The verdict can be recorded by:

- Token-based antiforgery middleware added by `app.UseAntiforgery()` (explicit usage).
- Automatic cross-origin CSRF protection middleware added by default to apps built with `WebApplication.CreateBuilder`.

Blazor SSR endpoints no longer call `IAntiforgery.ValidateRequestAsync` directly. Antiforgery tokens are generated only when token-based antiforgery middleware ran for the request.

Apps using `app.UseAntiforgery()` retain token-based validation. Apps without it rely on automatic cross-origin CSRF protection and no longer emit antiforgery tokens for their forms.


### Type of breaking change

- [ ] **Binary incompatible**: Existing binaries may encounter a breaking change in behavior, such as failure to load or execute, and if so, require recompilation.
- [ ] **Source incompatible**: When recompiled using the new SDK or component or to target the new runtime, existing source code may require source changes to compile successfully.
- [x] **Behavioral change**: Existing binaries may behave differently at run time.

### Reason for change

Token-based antiforgery and automatic cross-origin CSRF protection now record a shared verdict through `IAntiforgeryValidationFeature`.

Validating again inside the Blazor SSR endpoint duplicated work and could produce a result different from the middleware verdict. Generating tokens without token-based antiforgery middleware also produced tokens that nothing validated.

### Recommended action

If your Blazor SSR app relies on antiforgery tokens for form validation or rendering, ensure that it calls `app.UseAntiforgery()`:
```csharp
var app = builder.Build();

app.UseAntiforgery();
```

If you were not calling `app.UseAntiforgery()` before you will start using CSRF protection as the defense mechanism from now on.

### Affected APIs

None. This is a behavioral change affecting Blazor SSR form processing and antiforgery-token generation.

# ASP.NET Core 2.3 will reach end of support on April 13, 2027

> Update: The ASP.NET Core 2.3 end of support date was updated from April 7, 2027 to April 13, 2027 to align with the Microsoft servicing release cycles.

Today we are announcing that ASP.NET Core 2.3 will reach **end of support on April 13, 2027**. After that date, Microsoft will no longer provide security patches, bug fixes, or technical support for ASP.NET Core 2.3.

This announcement provides the required 12 months of advance notice, as defined by the [Microsoft Support Lifecycle Policy](https://learn.microsoft.com/lifecycle/faq/general-lifecycle#what-is-the-lifecycle-policy-for-tools-) for products classified as "Tools."

## Current support policy

ASP.NET Core 2.3 packages (latest patched version only) are currently [supported](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/platform/support/policy/aspnet#dotnet-core) on .NET Framework, following the support cycle for those .NET Framework versions. After April 13, 2027, this support will end regardless of the .NET Framework version in use.

Note that the [ASP.NET Core 2.3 packages](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/en-us/platform/support/policy/aspnet/2.3-packages) include the Entity Framework 2.3 packages, which will end support on the same date.

## Impact of end of support

After ASP.NET Core 2.3 reaches end of support:

- No new security updates will be issued for ASP.NET Core 2.3.
- Continuing to use an unsupported version may expose your applications to security vulnerabilities.
- Technical support will no longer be available for ASP.NET Core 2.3.
- The ASP.NET Core 2.3 packages will be deprecated.

## Upgrade recommendation

We recommend upgrading to a [currently supported version of .NET](https://dotnet.microsoft.com/download/dotnet), such as .NET 10 (LTS).

To help with the upgrade process, we recommend using [GitHub Copilot modernization](https://learn.microsoft.com/dotnet/core/porting/github-copilot-app-modernization/overview), which provides AI-powered assistance to help you analyze, plan, and execute your migration to a modern .NET version.
